records.region: Delta Amacuro, Tucupita–Macareo corridor of the Orinoco delta
records.candidate_name_role: Representative name of the receiving waterway system; not a uniform name assigned to every selected upstream reach.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected upper and middle Caño Tucupita corridor connects into the named lower Caño Macareo and continues to its coastal outlet. Caño Macareo is supported as the practical receiving-system representative; Tucupita remains a separate bounded reach name, and Barra de Macareo is the terminal setting rather than a river alias.
records.completion_scope: All selected stored parts, role/stage, opening, successive receiving channels, junction, wetland-channel passage and separate source/render endings are covered at useful ordinary geographic scale. No material through-link remains open. No additional imagery acquisition is needed for this bounded pass.
records.supported_name_scope: The selected upper and middle Caño Tucupita corridor connects into the named lower Caño Macareo and continues to its coastal outlet. Caño Macareo is supported as the practical receiving-system representative; Tucupita remains a separate bounded reach name, and Barra de Macareo is the terminal setting rather than a river alias.

scope_limits: Caño Tucupita and Caño Macareo are separate reach names, not true aliases. Caño Macareo represents the receiving system rather than a proven uniform name for the whole selected composite.
The cartographic name-transition scope is bounded by labeled waterways and their mapped junction; no official vertex-based naming boundary or formal registry entry was verified.
The selected opening is a model beginning within the northeastern Tucupita-side delta channel, not an established natural source. The unselected western and southern network is not silently added.

The source endpoint lies in the lower Macareo coastal approach, while the rendered endpoint extends farther toward the Barra de Macareo opening. Both occupy the continuously depicted receiving corridor; exact modern banks or tidal limits are not claimed.

The original chart is historical and generalized. Present tidal direction, flow, wetness, navigation and water-management operation remain unverified and are unnecessary for this ordinary geographic correspondence.

bounded_name_observations.name: Caño Tucupita
bounded_name_observations.scope: Directly labeled upper-to-middle selected northeastern channel, including its continuation beyond the road-adjacent opening toward the lower Macareo receiving join. The source does not establish a formal vertex for the name boundary.

bounded_name_observations.name: Caño Macareo
bounded_name_observations.scope: Directly labeled broad lower selected receiving corridor and its northward then northwestward continuation to the coast. Also used as the representative receiving-system identity, without renaming Tucupita.

bounded_name_observations.name: Barra de Macareo
bounded_name_observations.scope: Directly labeled coastal receiving opening at the selected final Macareo passage; not a synonym for the entire river group.

records.naming_scope_hold_reason: No hydronym is assigned. Full ordinary geographic correspondence is supported, but the material read does not place an attested river name on this exact selected composite. This does not assert that the waters are officially nameless.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No hydronym is assigned. Full ordinary geographic correspondence is supported, but the material read does not place an attested river name on this exact selected composite. This does not assert that the waters are officially nameless.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research is complete as a null name-scope hold. All one fragment,27 stored parts,stage3 and mainstem role were accounted for. No concrete geographic through-link remains missing. Optional report access restrictions remain recorded separately. No accepted name, automatic application or product/geometry change is authorized or made.
records.supported_name_scope: No hydronym is assigned. Full ordinary geographic correspondence is supported, but the material read does not place an attested river name on this exact selected composite. This does not assert that the waters are officially nameless.

scope_limits: No direct name labels occur in the imagery. The upper lakes, feeder and downstream reaches remain unassigned in this finding.
The Foucault River field mention is retained solely as a regional lead; it is not promoted to a whole-feature candidate or an alias.
Geographic correspondence is ordinary corridor-scale interpretation. Exact banks, current flow, lake levels, scene dates, tidal limits and legal name boundaries are not established.
The coastal source endpoint and farther rendered extension are separate; no selected path beyond the actual rendered ending was added.
Unavailable report content and discovery snippets are not substantive evidence. Inherited Canadian source holds were preserved, without inferring a ban on all independent Canadian sources.

bounded_name_observations.name: Foucault River
bounded_name_observations.observation: The museum field transcript names Foucault River in the Salluit study setting. It gives no exact geographic placement sufficient to attach the name to a selected component or the whole composite.

records.region: Pacific Colombia, Cauca: selected inland Guapi-area trunk, eastern contributing branch and northern tidal receiving corridor.
records.material_pending_reason: Independent visible coverage does not establish the chosen eastern opening through the substantially cloud-covered upper westward connection. Parts9–11 offer only intermittent exposed pieces, insufficient to bridge parts1–8.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No completed representative is assigned while the selected eastern opening has an unestablished geographic through-link. Guapi and the separately named lower branches remain bounded literature observations below.
records.completion_scope: The bounded pass covers all four FIDs and all66 stored parts. Ordinary correspondence is supported for the exposed western upper trunk, the northward middle trunk, selected tributary and its confluence, lower division and actual source/render endpoint settings. The eastern opening remains a real source-material gap, so the whole selection is not complete.
records.supported_name_scope: No completed representative is assigned while the selected eastern opening has an unestablished geographic through-link. Guapi and the separately named lower branches remain bounded literature observations below.

scope_limits: The eastern opening remains unconnected by adequately visible independent evidence.
The imagery is unnamed. Literature supports regional names and separate branches, but no precise upper-name transition or whole-composite uniform name is asserted.
The source and rendered terminal are inner-estuarine positions; model sea classification is not an independent shoreline observation.
Historic publication restrictions remain in force at their recorded scopes. No re-acquisition, alternate host, equivalent edition or unread-output recovery clears them.
The known old private record is incomplete; no claim is made that every historical publication identity has been recovered.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Guapi
bounded_name_observations.scope: The IIAP authorial account names the river and describes its division into the Guapi and Limones arms. The 2009 field report independently describes Guapi coastal watercourses. This is a bounded regional receiving-system lead, not a verified name for the cloud-obscured chosen opening or the whole selected composite.

bounded_name_observations.name: brazo Limones
bounded_name_observations.scope: The IIAP account identifies Limones as an arm of the Guapi bifurcation. The 2009 field report also uses the Limones arm in its Guajuí coastal discussion. The northward selected distributary is geographically visible, but the prose alone is not treated as a precise map-label placement or a whole-feature alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: brazo Guapi
bounded_name_observations.scope: Named separately from Limones in the IIAP account; retained for disambiguation, not as an alias for every selected lower reach.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Guajuí
bounded_name_observations.scope: The 2009 field study and IIAP basin account distinguish Guajuí in the coastal network. Its name is not extended to the selected inland trunk or used as an alias for Guapi.

concrete_material_gaps.gap: Independent visible coverage does not establish the chosen eastern opening through the substantially cloud-covered upper westward connection. Parts9–11 offer only intermittent exposed pieces, insufficient to bridge parts1–8.
concrete_material_gaps.needed_material: A permitted, independently identified original map or adequately clear photographic coverage of that specific upper connection. A river-name list, basin membership, discovery snippet or the selected geometry itself would not close it.
concrete_material_gaps.effect: One source-material-pending primary state. No full representative name, completed null scope hold or false through-link is assigned.

source_and_render_terminal_scope.source_ending: Final northward tidal-branch bend, southwest of the wider receiving junction.
source_and_render_terminal_scope.render_ending: Farther northeast in the wider estuarine receiving channel at the junction.
source_and_render_terminal_scope.tributary_source_and_render_ending: Coincident at its mainstem confluence; not the last mainstem endpoint.
source_and_render_terminal_scope.geographic_limit: Observed estuarine setting is retained separately from the model terminal class. No claim of exact contemporary shoreline alignment or current tide/flow state.

records.region: Sonora, Mexico: interior dry tributary corridor, western receiving valley, southern cultivated coastal plain and estuarine ending.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Complete photographic geographic correspondence does not establish a whole-composite or representative river-system hydronym. No naming original was read; discovery snippets are not substituted for it.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No river-system hydronym is supported by an actually read naming original in this bounded pass. Search-discovery labels and unread originals are excluded.
records.completion_scope: Three overlapping photographic views cover all 19 selected parts, the chosen opening, the westward and southward receiving corridors, modified coastal floor and both separately recorded terminal settings. Geographic correspondence is complete at ordinary corridor scale. The river-system name remains unestablished because no permitted naming original was actually read.
records.supported_name_scope: No river-system hydronym is supported by an actually read naming original in this bounded pass. Search-discovery labels and unread originals are excluded.

scope_limits: No actually read source supports a representative river-system name or a named tributary, bay or estuary assignment for this selection. Search-result names were discovery only and are not candidate evidence.

The selected coastal floor contains rectilinear ponds, embankments and managed-looking channels. Ordinary receiving geography is established without determining present hydraulic operation or passage through each structure.
The dry and locally diffuse agricultural plain is one continuous receiving floor at the inspected scale; absence of a continuously wet thread is not a material geographic gap.
The source and render endpoint settings differ and are described separately. No official mouth, exact modern bank or source-to-render geometry correction is claimed.
No original naming map or prose was read from the three unsuccessful optional publications. Their failures constrain naming evidence but do not create an additional geographic-pending classification.

terminal_observations.source_endpoint_setting: Marine side west-northwest of the estuarine opening and rendered endpoint.
terminal_observations.render_endpoint_setting: Southern margin of the western lagoon basin, east of the coast opening.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
